## Tenant Repair Request for Toronto Apartment

Here’s a polite but firm message you can send to your landlord, plus a simple maintenance checklist and a communication log template. I’ve assumed you want a professional tone, a clear 7-day repair request, and wording suitable for a 2-bedroom rental in Toronto.

## Draft Email and Maintenance Checklist

**Subject:** Urgent Repair Request: Kitchen Sink Leak, Slow Bathtub Drain, and Bedroom Window Latch

Dear [Landlord’s Name],

I’m writing to follow up on the maintenance issues in my 2-bedroom apartment at [address/unit number]. I first reported these concerns **5 days ago**, but I have not yet received a response.

The following repairs are needed:
- Leaking kitchen sink
- Slow-draining bathtub
- Broken bedroom window latch

These issues are affecting the safe and comfortable use of the apartment, and I would appreciate a prompt response. Please arrange for the repairs to be completed within **7 days** of this email, or let me know when a technician will be coming to inspect and fix them.

If needed, I can provide photos or allow access to the unit with reasonable notice. Thank you for your attention to this matter, and I look forward to hearing from you soon.

Sincerely,
[Your full name]
[Your phone number]
[Your email address]
[Unit/address]

### Maintenance Checklist
- Kitchen sink: check for active leak under faucet, drain, and supply lines
- Bathtub: clear drain blockage; test drainage speed after cleaning
- Bedroom window latch: inspect latch alignment, locking function, and frame fit
- Water damage: look for cabinet swelling, mold, or staining near sink
- Safety check: confirm bedroom window can close and secure properly
- Follow-up record: note dates, times, and any responses from landlord or contractor

### Communication Log Template
- Date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Time: [HH:MM]
- Contact method: [Email / Phone / Text / In person]
- Person contacted: [Name]
- Issue reported: [Brief description]
- Response received: [What they said]
- Next step promised: [Inspection / repair date / no response]
- Follow-up needed by: [Date]
- Notes: [Photos sent, access arranged, further damage observed]

## Toronto Tenant Follow-Up Plan

If the landlord still does not respond after this email, keep everything in writing and continue documenting the issues. A clear paper trail helps if you need to escalate the matter through tenant support channels.

- Send the email by both email and text if possible
- Attach dated photos or short videos of each issue
- Save screenshots of all messages and missed calls
- Keep a dated log of any water damage, odors, or worsening drainage
- If the window latch affects security, mention that specifically in your follow-up

## Quick Actions
